description: Use this when someone asks how much a travel eSIM costs in a country or region, what the average or typical price is, or how much choice there is, before comparing individual plans. Returns the number of plans and providers listed on the MyBestSim comparison page, typical prices computed over all of them (median price of standard packages: 1 GB/7 days, 5, 10 and 20 GB/30 days, unlimited 7 and 30 days; median price per GB), the cheapest plan, the best price per GB, the cheapest unlimited plan if any, the available validities, and the link to the comparison page. Pass currency when you know the traveller's.

currency.description: Currency to show prices in (ISO 4217, e.g. "EUR", "GBP", "USD"): pass the traveller's currency whenever you know it (their country, their words, prices they quoted). Default: the currency of the MyBestSim page in the conversation language (EUR for fr, de, es, it, nl, pt…; USD for en; GBP is never assumed). Prices are converted exactly as that page shows them.

destination.description: Where the traveller is going, as they named it: a country in English or another common language ("Japan", "Japon"), an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code ("JP"), a well-known city ("Tokyo"), or one of the regions Europe, Asia, Africa, North America, South America, World, Balkans. Never the traveller's home country.

language.description: Language of the conversation (ISO 639-1). Links open our comparison page in that language when it exists, otherwise in English. Default "en".

name: get_destination_overview

dataGb.description: Total data in GB; null when unlimited.

price.description: Price in the response currency, as the MyBestSim page shows it.

pricePerGb.description: Price per GB in the response currency; null when unlimited.

unlimited.description: True for an unlimited-data plan. Its fair-use policy is not published here: present it as "Unlimited" without inventing a cap.

anyOf.description: Typical prices on the comparison page, computed over ALL its plans (never a sample), in the response currency. For each standard package: median, lowest and highest price of the plans with exactly that data and validity (unlimited: any unlimited plan of that validity); planCount 0 = no such plan, prices null. medianPricePerGb: median of price ÷ GB over every fixed-data plan. Use these for "average" or "typical" price questions; a median is the middle plan, not the mean.
